title: Molecular Machines
description: At a molecule's scale everything shakes, so a machine cannot push: it must ratchet. Feringa's motor turns by light twisting a double bond, then by heat flipping its crowded halves past each other, always one way because the other way is uphill: two flashes and two flips a turn, the slowest setting the pace. Each flip is a barrier crossed at Eyring's rate, kT/h times e to the minus ΔG‡ over RT. A rotaxane is a ring threaded on an axle and stoppered, which can be made to shuttle between stations. Unlocks the Molecular Machine Bench.

puzzle.goal: A barrier ΔG per mole is crossed at temperature T. Write the rate k by transition state theory, with kB/h the ratio of Boltzmann's to Planck's constant (Eyring).
puzzle.name: Eyring equation
puzzle.form: c * T * exp ( - G / ( R * T ) )
puzzle.expr: c * T * exp ( - G / ( R * T ) )
puzzle.ask: Find k in /s for c = kB/h = 2.0837e10, ΔG = 70000 J/mol, R = 8.314 and T = @{T} K.
puzzle.method: The transition state is in equilibrium with the start, K‡ = e^(−ΔG‡/RT), and falls apart at the frequency of one vibration, kT/h.
